display.name: PagerDuty
display.blurb: Triage incidents, inspect services and escalation policies, and see who's on call — driven by the `pd` CLI over the PagerDuty REST API v2. The API token is brokered: injected at the egress proxy, never seen by the agent.

cli.doc:
Use `pd` to drive PagerDuty from this session — triage incidents, inspect services / schedules / escalation policies, and see who's on call (REST API v2). Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects the brokered API token on every request to api.pagerduty.com; `PAGERDUTY_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder. Do NOT set a real token or run any login. The CLI sends the required `Accept: application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2` header for you. Calls to a path your profile didn't grant are denied at the network boundary, not authenticated.

Subcommands (each needs the matching power on your profile):
  pd incidents [field=value ...]   List incidents — `pd incidents statuses[]=triggered statuses[]=acknowledged` (incidents:read).
  pd incident <id>                 Get one incident by ID (incidents:read).
  pd ack <id>                      Acknowledge an incident — PUT /incidents (incidents:write).
  pd resolve <id>                  Resolve an incident — PUT /incidents (incidents:write).
  pd services [field=value ...]    List services (services:read).
  pd schedules [field=value ...]   List on-call schedules (schedules:read).
  pd oncalls [field=value ...]     Who is on call now — `pd oncalls` or filter `pd oncalls schedule_ids[]=PXXXXXX` (oncalls:read).
  pd policies [field=value ...]    List escalation policies (escalation_policies:read).
  pd users [field=value ...]       List users (users:read).
  pd whoami                        Probe auth via GET /abilities.
  pd get <path> [field=value ...]  Raw GET: `pd get /incidents since=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` (uses the power matching the path).
  pd api <METHOD> <path> [json]    Raw call: `pd api POST /incidents '{"incident":{...}}'` (needs the :write power for that resource).

Notes: list endpoints paginate with `limit` and `offset`. Writes to /incidents (`pd ack`/`pd resolve`, and creating incidents via `pd api POST /incidents`) require PagerDuty's `From` header naming a requester email — set `PD_FROM=you@your-org.com` in the environment and the CLI adds it; without it the write returns a 400. The API replies with JSON; non-2xx bodies carry an `error` object.
